description: Apply Pearl's framework for causal reasoning — the Ladder of Causation, causal diagrams (DAGs), and the structural distinction between good and bad controls — when the user is asking a cause-and-effect question. Use whenever the user asks "does X cause Y", interprets a study or A/B test, asks "should I control for [variable]" or which covariates to include, encounters Simpson's paradox or a sign reversal, evaluates observational data, considers a natural experiment or instrumental variable, works with regression discontinuity, differences-in-differences, panel/longitudinal data, or asks about heterogeneous treatment effects across user segments — even if they don't say "causal." Common cases include experiment design, regression interpretation, policy evaluation, and questions about confounding or selection bias.
